correctness.rationale: For odd common prime p>7 at offsets difference d<=7, subtraction and substitution force p|d²+4. Only separations 3,5,7 can be hit by primes other than 2,5. With factor 2, one parity is covered and the other cannot be covered by two remaining factors; without factor 2, factor 5 must cover four positions and its two four-hit complements have no matching into allowed two-hit prime pairs. The seven-position example and the CRT infinite family are exact. Finite exhaustive local masks independently corroborate but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A natural polynomial Jacobsthal-style sieve invariant with a fixed three-prime support has a uniform, sharp, nonobvious ceiling independent of the size or powers of its prime divisors. The proof isolates exactly which primes can hit two of eight consecutive quadratic values and reduces the obstruction to a rigid two-edge matching, while the CRT gives infinitely many sharp moduli. This is a meaningful finite covering boundary rather than an arbitrary numerical sample.
